item.title: Pedestrian airlifted to Pensacola hospital after Baldwin County garbage truck crash
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The severity of the crash prompted a helicopter response to the scene. Details about the exact location on U.S. Highway and the pedestrian's current condition were not immediately available.…
item.content:encoded:
A pedestrian was airlifted to a Pensacola hospital Thursday after being struck by a garbage truck in Baldwin County, Alabama, according to WKRG News 5.

The severity of the crash prompted a helicopter response to the scene. Details about the exact location on U.S. Highway and the pedestrian's current condition were not immediately available.

Baldwin County officials coordinated the emergency airlift, with the patient transported to a Pensacola-area medical facility for treatment. The incident underscores the hazards pedestrians face around heavy commercial vehicles, particularly along busy roadways.

item.content:encoded:
The Foley Public Library is gearing up for its third annual Big Rigs at the Library event this October, bringing heavy equipment, live entertainment, and interactive activities to the Baldwin County community.

According to city officials, the touch-a-truck event will feature an array of vehicles including tractors, backhoes, and bucket trucks that children can see up close. The family-friendly outing will also include a petting zoo and live music, creating a full day of activities for the region.

The event has grown since its first year, establishing itself as a popular October tradition for families looking to get hands-on with machinery and equipment they don't often encounter in everyday life. Details on specific dates and times are expected to be announced soon.

item.content:encoded: A home in Escambia County was destroyed by fire Saturday afternoon after being struck by lightning, according to Escambia County Fire Rescue. The fire broke out shortly before 4 p.m. on September 12, officials said. While the home sustained significant damage, no additional details about injuries or the specific location within the county were immediately available. The incident underscores the fire risks posed by lightning strikes during severe weather, particularly as hurricane season peaks in the coming weeks.

item.title: Atlantic disturbance could develop into tropical depression this week
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The National Hurricane Center is monitoring a subtropical Atlantic disturbance that has the potential to become a tropical depression in the coming days, according to WKRG News 5. While the system remains in the open Atlantic, residents and businesses across the Gulf Coast should keep tabs on the National Hurricane Center's updates as the system…
item.content:encoded:
The National Hurricane Center is monitoring a subtropical Atlantic disturbance that has the potential to become a tropical depression in the coming days, according to WKRG News 5.

While the system remains in the open Atlantic, residents and businesses across the Gulf Coast should keep tabs on the National Hurricane Center's updates as the system develops. Even disturbances that don't immediately threaten land can shift course or intensify rapidly during Atlantic storm season.

The weather service will issue routine updates on the disturbance's position and development potential. Pensacola-area residents can monitor the latest forecasts through the National Weather Service office in Mobile or the National Hurricane Center's website for any changes that could affect Northwest Florida.

item.title: Free car seat safety checks offered in Bay Minette
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Bay Minette Fire Department and North Baldwin Infirmary are joining forces to provide free car seat safety inspections for families in the area. item.content:encoded:
The Bay Minette Fire Department and North Baldwin Infirmary are joining forces to provide free car seat safety inspections for families in the area. The program aims to ensure children and infants are properly secured during vehicle travel, addressing a critical public safety concern that affects young passengers across Baldwin County and the surrounding region.

According to WKRG News 5, certified technicians will be available to check car seats for proper installation and correct usage, helping parents identify potential safety issues before they become dangerous. Improper car seat installation remains a leading cause of injury and death among young children in traffic accidents.

This type of community partnership has proven effective in other areas, combining emergency services expertise with healthcare resources to reach families who might not otherwise have access to professional safety guidance. Residents interested in participating can contact the Bay Minette Fire Department or North Baldwin Infirmary for scheduling details and specific dates for the safety checks.

item.title: Nearly 2 inches of rain swamps downtown Pensacola drainage system
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A thunderstorm pounded downtown Pensacola with nearly two inches of rain in just 30 minutes over the weekend, leaving the area's drainage system unable to keep up with the deluge. According to WKRG News 5, the intense rainfall overwhelmed storm drains in the downtown corridor, creating localized flooding across streets and low-lying areas. The…
item.content:encoded:
A thunderstorm pounded downtown Pensacola with nearly two inches of rain in just 30 minutes over the weekend, leaving the area's drainage system unable to keep up with the deluge.

According to WKRG News 5, the intense rainfall overwhelmed storm drains in the downtown corridor, creating localized flooding across streets and low-lying areas. The rapid precipitation rate exceeded what the existing drainage infrastructure could handle in such a compressed timeframe.

The incident highlights ongoing concerns about Pensacola's drainage capacity during heavy downpours, a recurring issue in the downtown area during severe weather events. City officials have previously identified stormwater management as a priority, particularly in older sections of downtown where drainage systems date back decades.

No injuries were reported from the event, though the flooding may have caused temporary road closures and property impacts in affected neighborhoods.

item.title: Escambia Man Sentenced for Selling Illegal Gun Conversion Devices Online
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A 22-year-old Escambia County man has pleaded guilty in federal court to illegally selling machine gun conversion devices through Facebook, according to court records. Alaisjah Dayshawn Perkins admitted to receiving, possessing, transferring, and manufacturing unregistered firearms—devices that convert standard weapons into fully automatic…
item.content:encoded:
A 22-year-old Escambia County man has pleaded guilty in federal court to illegally selling machine gun conversion devices through Facebook, according to court records.

Alaisjah Dayshawn Perkins admitted to receiving, possessing, transferring, and manufacturing unregistered firearms—devices that convert standard weapons into fully automatic weapons—without proper serial numbers or federal registration. The charges carry serious federal penalties related to National Firearms Registration and Transfer Record violations.

The case underscores ongoing federal enforcement efforts targeting illegal firearms trafficking on social media platforms. Unregistered conversion devices are illegal under federal law and pose significant public safety concerns. Perkins' sentencing is pending, with a judge to determine his penalty at a later hearing.

item.title: West Roberts Road Reopening Delayed to Thursday; Full Project Won't Finish Until Winter

The temporary closure, which began August 29, has now extended well beyond initial expectations. Crews now anticipate reopening the affected portion by 5…
item.content:encoded:
A stretch of West Roberts Road in North Escambia that shut down for construction work back in August will finally reopen by Thursday evening, weather permitting, according to project officials.

The temporary closure, which began August 29, has now extended well beyond initial expectations. Crews now anticipate reopening the affected portion by 5 p.m. Thursday, but that's just one piece of a larger undertaking.

The overall West Roberts Road project won't be finished until winter, meaning drivers in the area should expect continued work and potential delays in the coming months. The extension underscores the complexity of the construction effort and the challenges crews have faced since work began nearly three months ago.

item.title: Blue Wahoos Celebrate Decade With Northview Grad Brianna Smith
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Blue Wahoos recently recognized Brianna Smith for a milestone most fans might overlook—ten years of twirling as the team's beloved "Twirly Girl." Smith, a 2017 Northview High School graduate, has been a fixture at Blue Wahoos games, performing with fiery batons in a role that's become part of the ballpark experience for many local…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos recently recognized Brianna Smith for a milestone most fans might overlook—ten years of twirling as the team's beloved "Twirly Girl."

Smith, a 2017 Northview High School graduate, has been a fixture at Blue Wahoos games, performing with fiery batons in a role that's become part of the ballpark experience for many local fans. Before joining the professional team, she made a name for herself as a majorette at Northview, where her baton work caught attention both in the stands and around town.

These days, Smith balances her Blue Wahoos appearances with a full-time career in education. She's in her fourth year teaching at Byrneville Elementary School, where she brings that same energy and skill to her students. The recognition from the Blue Wahoos is a nod to her decade of dedication and the role she's played in the team's game-day tradition.

item.content:encoded:
Expect another hot day across the Pensacola area Tuesday, with highs climbing to around 93 degrees and plenty of sunshine. Winds will stay calm early, then shift to the east at around 5 mph during the morning hours.

Tuesday night will cool down to around 74 degrees under mostly clear skies, with east winds continuing at about 5 mph after midnight.

The hot pattern continues into Wednesday, when sunny skies will accompany highs near 90 degrees. If you're heading outdoors, remember to stay hydrated and use sun protection during peak afternoon hours.

item.title: FDOT Seeks Input on Highway 29 and 196 Safety Options Tonight
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Transportation is hosting a public meeting this evening to get community feedback on safety improvements planned for the intersection of Highway 29 and Highway 196 (Barrineau Park Road) in North Escambia. Residents will have the chance to weigh in on two competing proposals for the busy intersection. One option calls for…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Transportation is hosting a public meeting this evening to get community feedback on safety improvements planned for the intersection of Highway 29 and Highway 196 (Barrineau Park Road) in North Escambia.

Residents will have the chance to weigh in on two competing proposals for the busy intersection. One option calls for installing a traditional traffic signal, while the other would implement what's known as a Restricted Crossing U-Turn, or RCUT — a less common traffic control method that has gained attention in recent years as a safety alternative.

The meeting gives area drivers and property owners a direct line to state transportation officials before any final decision is made. If you live or work near the intersection and want your voice heard on the project, the public meeting is your opportunity to provide input on which approach you think is best for the area.

item.title: Alabama City Pumps Brakes on Data Centers Before Projects Arrive
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Foley, Alabama is hitting pause on data center development to get ahead of the artificial intelligence boom sweeping the country. City leaders want to establish regulations before any projects are even proposed, according to WKRG News 5. Mayor Ralph Hellmich said the city is being proactive. "We wanted to make sure our city was prepared," he told…
item.content:encoded:
Foley, Alabama is hitting pause on data center development to get ahead of the artificial intelligence boom sweeping the country. City leaders want to establish regulations before any projects are even proposed, according to WKRG News 5.

Mayor Ralph Hellmich said the city is being proactive. "We wanted to make sure our city was prepared," he told the station. The move reflects growing concern among municipalities nationwide about how to manage the rapid expansion of data centers needed to power AI applications.

Foley joins other communities taking a cautious approach to data center growth. The facilities are energy-intensive and can strain local infrastructure, water supplies, and power grids. By establishing a regulatory framework now, Foley hopes to attract responsible development while protecting city resources.

The conversation in Foley may serve as a model for other Gulf Coast communities facing similar pressures. As tech companies race to build out AI infrastructure, local governments are learning they need clear rules in place before developers come knocking.
